Delhi, India's vibrant capital, is a world within itself. With its kaleidoscope of scents, sounds, and sights, Delhi never fails to captivate. From its rich history and architectural marvels to its delectable cuisine and vibrant nightlife, the city offers an unforgettable experience.

One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, Delhi’s roots date back to the era of the ancient Mahabharata, when the city was known as Indraprastha, the legendary home of the Pandavas. Since then, the city has seen empires rise and fall, from the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals, who left behind architectural marvels, to the British, who shaped parts of it.

While Delhi is a melting pot of varied cultures, what sets it apart is its diverse character. Here, you can experience the best of both worlds—the timeless elegance of a bygone era alongside the exhilarating energy of a modern megacity. On the one hand, you’ll find the vibrant chaos of narrow lanes, centuries-old monuments, and old-world charm. On the other, the city offers vast green spaces, modern buildings, swanky malls, and colonial-era architecture.

Delhi wears the marks of time like a badge of honour. Home to eight historic cities, this ancient city has been built, destroyed, and rebuilt several times, each chapter adding a new layer to its story.

Delhi’s skyline is adorned with three incredible UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The iconic Red Fort , or Lal Quila, is simply an unmissable attraction of the city. Built by Emperor Shah Jahan in the 17 th century, this red sandstone fortress is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture, a remarkable blend of Indian, Persian, and European influences that will leave you breathless. Don't miss the fort’s evening sound and light show, Jai Hind—a dazzling spectacle that brings its history to life.

You must visit the Qutub Minar , a 12 th -century red and buff sandstone tower that symbolises Delhi's early Islamic heritage. And then, there’s the mesmerising Humayun's Tomb , a 16 th -century garden mausoleum that marries Mughal craftsmanship with a stunning octagonal design. Its symmetrical layout and serene environs will transport you to another time.

Prepare to be blown away by more heritage wonders in Delhi, such as the majestic India Gate , a poignant symbol of Indian courage, patriotism, and sacrifice. Explore the imposing National War Memorial that pays tribute to India's gallant Armed Forces. Unlock the mysteries of time and space at Jantar Mantar, an intriguing observatory teeming with ancient astronomical instruments.

If you love to go beyond the usual tourist trails and discover hidden gems instead, Delhi has got you covered, too. Explore Agrasen Ki Baoli, an intricately designed stepwell believed to have been constructed during the era of the Mahabharata, or visit the Mirza Ghalib Ki Haveli, the historic mansion of one of India's most celebrated Urdu poets. In for some quirky adventure? Check out the spooky Bhuli Bhatiyari ka Mahal situated within the Central Ridge Reserve Forest. For a treasure trove of history, don’t miss the grand Mehrauli Archaeological Park, where you’ll find monuments from the Sultanate era to the Mughals and the British.

Beyond its historical landmarks, Delhi is a city steeped in spirituality. From serene temples to grand mosques, the city offers a haven for the soul. Visit the majestic Akshardham Temple dedicated to Lord Swaminarayan or feel the energy as you walk amongst pilgrims and devotees at the Nizamuddin Dargah, a revered shrine dedicated to Sufi saint Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya. Experience the soul-stirring qawwali sessions, where Sufi music and poetry come alive in their most enchanting form!

Visit Jama Masjid , one of India's largest mosques, standing as a testament to architectural excellence. Discover the ancient Sri Digambar Jain Lal Temple near the Red Fort, the oldest Jain sanctuary known for its distinctive Jain Birds Hospital. Don't miss the vibrant Sikh culture at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib , a prominent gurdwara known for its stunning architecture and langar (community kitchen) that serves all who come. Seeking a moment of quiet reflection? Find it at the Lotus Temple , a unique architectural wonder shaped like a lotus flower, as its tranquil embrace welcomes all faiths.

Whether you're a seasoned foodie or simply looking for a new culinary adventure, Delhi is always ready to delight your senses. From tantalising street food to trendy cafes and award-winning restaurants serving global cuisine, the city has everything to satiate the foodie in you.

But if there’s anything quintessential Delhi, it is its lip-smacking street food. Zesty chaats, sizzling tikkis, flaky parathas, delectable butter chicken, succulent kebabs, tangy gol gappe, and wholesome chole bhature – an array of gastronomic treasures await you! While these treats are found all over Delhi, some spots deserve special mention. Dive headfirst into Chandni Chowk , the heart of Old Delhi, for a sensory overload of spices, sweets, and street food. Craving variety? Visit Connaught Place – a swarming hub that offers a global culinary adventure. For a modern take on Indian flavours, explore trendy neighbourhoods like Khan Market and Hauz Khas Village. So, come hungry, come curious!

Get ready to unleash your inner shopaholic and discover the lively shopping scene of Delhi. Here, gleaming malls stand side-by-side with vibrant bazaars, and brand outlets share the stage with quirky stores. Clothing, accessories, jewellery, exquisite décor, or one-of-a-kind furniture – you name it and Delhi has it.

Experience the city like a local by browsing vibrant markets like Connaught Place, Chandni Chowk, Lajpat Nagar, Khan Market, and Sarojini Nagar. These shopping destinations double as social hubs bustling with a contagious energy that's simply delightful. Dilli Haat , a cultural haven, beckons souvenir hunters with its curated collection of handicrafts and regional specialities. Don’t miss Khari Baoli, Asia's largest spice market, a whirlwind of aromas and exotic ingredients. Bargaining is a Delhi shopping tradition (unless prices are fixed). So, hone your skills and score amazing deals!

If you’re a curious traveller, you’re in for a treat, as Delhi boasts some of the most distinctive museums in India. While the National Museum is where you can delve deep into the nation’s history, the Sulabh International Museum of Toilets offers a surprisingly quirky look at sanitation! Train buffs will love the National Rail Museum's collection of vintage locomotives, while doll enthusiasts can journey through global cultures at Shankar's International Dolls Museum. For a glimpse into Indian craftsmanship, the Crafts Museum awaits, housing an impressive collection of over 35,000 exquisite articles.

Delhi boasts hidden pockets of green that offer a welcome escape from the urban buzz. Discover lush oases and beloved picnic destinations, like Sunder Nursery, Lodhi Garden , and Garden of Five Senses , where you can simply surrender to nature. Explore the Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, a haven for wildlife that offers experiences like bird watching, nature walks, and a drive to a serene lake!

Another hidden side of Delhi is its artistic soul. A world of cultural centres, contemporary galleries and theatres promises an enriching experience for every art lover. Visit Mandi House, Kamani Auditorium, Shriram Bharatiya Kala Kendra, India Habitat Centre (IHC), The National Gallery of Modern Art and many more venues to experience the city at its artistic best. These spots are always buzzing with theatre shows, poetry readings, musicals, and film screenings. So, ditch the guidebooks for a while and dive into Delhi's creative energy!

Delhi unveils its best-kept secrets on foot. You can embark on heritage walks to uncover hidden gems and delve deeper into the city's rich past. Navigating the narrow lanes on a cycle rickshaw is a fun and authentic way to soak up the atmosphere. Need to cover larger distances? Hop on the swanky Delhi Metro, a clean and efficient lifeline connecting the city and nearby areas.

Delhi's magic unfolds in the cooler months (from October to March) when the weather is perfect for exploring—no scorching heat, just pleasant sunshine and blooming flowers! So, come and discover a city that has something for everyone, a city that will stay with you long after you depart.
The Red Fort was originally constructed with red and white colours, but the British later altered it to be entirely red.
The Qutub Minar is a towering minaret that was built in the 12 th century and is the tallest masonry tower in India!
The unique design of Lotus Temple resembles a blooming lotus flower and has won numerous architectural awards.
